title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array with Distinct Values
statement_md:
There is an integer array `nums` sorted in ascending order (with distinct values).

Prior to being passed to your function, `nums` is possibly rotated at an unknown pivot index `k` (`1 <= k < nums.length`) such that the resulting array is `[nums[k], nums[k+1], ..., nums[n-1], nums[0], nums[1], ..., nums[k-1]]`.

Given the array `nums` after the possible rotation and an integer `target`, return the index of `target` if it is in `nums`, or `-1` if it is not in `nums`.

You must write an algorithm with `O(log n)` runtime complexity.

### Input Format
- Line 1: A JSON-encoded list of integers `nums`
- Line 2: Integer `target`

### Output Format
- An integer representing index or -1

hints.text: In any rotated sorted array, dividing at mid produces at least one strictly sorted half.
Determine which half is sorted: if nums[left] <= nums[mid], left half is sorted; else right half is sorted.
Use Modified Binary Search checking if target falls within the bounds of the sorted half.

editorial_md:
### Optimal Approach: Partitioned Binary Search

Calculate `mid`. If `nums[left] <= nums[mid]`, left half is sorted. Check if `nums[left] <= target < nums[mid]`: if so, search left (`right = mid - 1`); else search right (`left = mid + 1`). Otherwise, right half is sorted: check if `nums[mid] < target <= nums[right]` and adjust bounds accordingly.

#### Complexity
- **Time Complexity:** $O(\log n)$ single binary search.
- **Space Complexity:** $O(1)$ constant memory.

#### Common Pitfalls
- Non-strict inequality when checking target range in sorted half.
